title: The Elon Times — EMAG exploration, November 27, 2026
headline: What Tesla filed to buy from EMAG — and what a ‘cartel office’ is
dek: On November 23 Tesla notified Germany’s Federal Cartel Office of an asset purchase from EMAG, a Swabian machine-tool maker. The notice became public November 27 as case B5-132/26. The machines do precision, electrochemical and laser work on metal. The filing does not say where Tesla would use them, and the review is still pending.
scope: Curious-exploration ledger story on tesla-emag-asset-acquisition-filed-bundeskartellamt-2026-11-23. Styling reused from fronts/ledger-story-2026-11-25/. Typographic share card only; no documentary or AI-generated images.
note: Facts are taken from the named ledger row, related ledger rows, and the sources listed here. Interpretation is labeled Chronicle’s read. events.json and published-stories.json were not modified. This folder has not been deployed.

unverified_or_incomplete.item: Purchase price and exact asset scope
unverified_or_incomplete.detail: The Bundeskartellamt notice lists an asset acquisition (Vermögenserwerb) and the product fields, but no price and no list of plants, machines, or contracts. Tesla and EMAG have not commented.

unverified_or_incomplete.item: About 220 EMAG staff moving to Tesla, and a prior robotics working relationship
unverified_or_incomplete.detail: Reported by Stuttgarter Nachrichten and Business Insider, via Electrek, Handelsblatt, and TeslaNorth. Neither company has confirmed the number or the purpose.

Business Insider, repeated by Electrek and Automotive World, reported a €42 million loss on €496 million of revenue in 2024 and 455 German job cuts, about 300 in Salach. SWR, citing the 2024 annual report, put the loss at about €43 million. Chronicle did not independently read the annual report.

unverified_or_incomplete.item: Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE managers and shell-company history
unverified_or_incomplete.detail: Electrek cites the German company register for HRB 315756, €120,000 capital, Austraße 24, Salach, and the August 26 ‘Blitz 26-299 SE’ origin. Manager names and roles come from Business Insider Germany as cited by Electrek and Handelsblatt. Chronicle did not pull the register extract itself.

unverified_or_incomplete.item: Which merger-control threshold applied, and the exact Phase 1 deadline
unverified_or_incomplete.detail: The office published a November 23 notification date. First phase is one month from a complete notification. Chronicle has not seen a statement that the file was deemed complete on that day, so a late-December first-phase date is a rule-of-thumb only. The notice does not say whether turnover or transaction-value thresholds triggered the filing.

unverified_or_incomplete.item: Tesla’s intended use of the equipment
unverified_or_incomplete.detail: The filing does not say. Tesla has not stated a purpose. Some German coverage implied a Tesla statement about robot parts; Chronicle could not verify any such statement and treats purpose as interpretation, not fact.

unverified_or_incomplete.item: Reuters original URL for the no-comment line
unverified_or_incomplete.detail: Automotive World attributes to Reuters that Tesla declined to comment and EMAG did not respond. Chronicle did not locate a working Reuters permalink.

The notice text was verified via the finanznachrichten.de reprint dated November 27, 2026, 09:30. Direct fetches of some Bundeskartellamt listing URLs failed or redirected. Official task, merger-control, and notification pages were retrieved.
Not used. The ledger has no official Tesla V3 unveiling. Secondary supply-chain reports have used the term; they are not a Tesla designation in the ledger.
